chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sukuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It was said to the Commander of the Believers (peace be upon him): What is abstinence in this world? He said: Avoiding its forbidden parts.

key_terms.الزَّهْدُ: Asceticism or abstinence from worldly desires
key_terms.حَرَامَهَا: Its forbidden parts (referring to haram acts within permissible worldly activities)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of zuhd (asceticism) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defining *zuhd* as avoiding the *haram* rather than total renunciation, a view that counters the extreme asceticism of the *Ghulat* and aligns with the Shia principle of balanced worldly engagement. This definition underscores that permissible (*halal*) worldly life is not only allowed but encouraged, provided one remains vigilant against prohibited elements, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Ali bin Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sukuni, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:
It was said to the Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him: What is abstinence in this world? He said: Avoiding from what is forbidden of it.
